note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address and opening time below comes from the City of Las Vegas's own pages: a parenthesis in each park page's amenity list, beneath a header that carries the address, the postcode and the park hours, and a City blog post of 11 March 2026 that names eight parks with a count each. Three of the five venues are counted on both records and the numbers agree. Two, Lorenzi and Patriot, are counted only on the post, and their own park pages never mention pickleball. The City states no lighting, no price, no surface and no indoor or outdoor for any venue, and where it is silent this page says so.

slots.parking:
The City of Las Vegas publishes nothing about parking at any of these five parks: not a lot, not a capacity, not a fee, not a permit. The same is true of restrooms. That is recorded as a silence rather than as a no, because an amenity list that names bocce and horseshoe courts, as Aloha Shores' does, is not obviously a complete list.

What the City does write is the size and shape of the sites. Centennial Hills is "a 120-acre state-of-the-art regional park" with soccer fields, a dog park and an amphitheatre. Durango Hills is built around an 18-hole executive golf course. Lorenzi has twin lakes and the Sammy Davis Jr. Festival Plaza. Patriot's page names a basketball court, tennis courts, a playground and picnic areas.
slots.peak_hours:
Las Vegas publishes one clock for every venue and it is a long one. Each of the five park pages gives park hours of 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. in its header, directly under the address.

How much of that window is usable after dark the City does not answer. Not one of the five pages, and not the pickleball post, says whether any pickleball court is lit. An 11 p.m. closing time is a fact about the gate, not about the lamps, so lighting at all nineteen courts is recorded as unknown.

No page names a busy period or a rotation rule. The nearest thing to a timing fact is the count: two courts at Centennial Hills or Patriot is one game, and seven at Durango Hills is a rotation.
slots.surface_condition:
The City of Las Vegas names a surface for a pickleball court nowhere. No page among the nine read for this city says what any court is made of, so all nineteen verified courts read as not stated on surface.

None says whether a court is indoor or outdoor either. The count is a parenthesis in an amenity list, "Pickleball courts (4)", sitting between "Volleyball courts" and "Playground". And none says whether a court is dedicated or lined onto a tennis court. Aloha Shores, Lorenzi and Patriot list tennis courts beside the pickleball; Centennial Hills and Durango Hills list none. Lorenzi's tennis courts are "managed by No Quit Tennis Academy", a fact about tennis that is not carried across to the pickleball courts.
slots.local_scene:
Nineteen verified courts across five City parks: seven at Durango Hills, four each at Aloha Shores and Lorenzi, and two each at Centennial Hills and Patriot. Las Vegas is the first Nevada city on this site and the first in Clark County.

The City's post of 11 March 2026 counts thirty-five courts at eight parks, so the published nineteen are a little over half of what the City says it has. The missing sixteen are named here rather than hidden: eight at Police Memorial Park, four at Bill Briare Family Park and four at Justice Myron Leavitt & Jaycee Community Park. Neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find "3250 Metro Academy Way" or "650 N. Tenaya Way", and the City publishes no address at all for the third.

The City states no price. Nothing on any page says a court is free or charges for one, so no Las Vegas venue is called free.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Durango Hills Park has seven pickleball courts, the largest published count in Las Vegas, stated twice by the City: "Pickleball courts (7)" on the park page and "Seven at Durango Hills Park" on its post. The park is built around the 18-hole executive Durango Hills Golf Club, with basketball courts and a skate park. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Seven is a rotation; lighting is not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a park the City describes by its pickleball
best_for.text: Aloha Shores Park is the one Las Vegas park page whose description names the game: "This neighborhood park features pickleball courts." Four courts, counted twice by the City, beside tennis, bocce, horseshoe and volleyball courts, a playground and a walk/jog track, at 7550 Sauer St. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Four courts is two games at once. Lighting and price are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play in a historic park
best_for.text: Lorenzi Park has four courts on the City's post and a park page that never mentions them, so this venue rests on one City record and says so. The park is on the City's Historic Property Register and the Nevada State Register of Historic Places: David G. Lorenzi's 80 acres, opened as Lorenzi's Lake Park in 1926, with twin lakes, a band shell and the Sammy Davis Jr. Festival Plaza.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Las Vegas have?
faqs.a: Nineteen across five City parks: 7 at Durango Hills, 4 at Aloha Shores, 4 at Lorenzi, 2 at Centennial Hills and 2 at Patriot. The City's post of 11 March 2026 counts 35 at eight parks; the other 16 are at addresses this site cannot resolve.

faqs.q: Which Las Vegas courts have lights?
faqs.a: None that the City states. No park page and not the pickleball post says a word about lighting at any pickleball court, and park hours of 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. are a fact about the gate rather than the lamps. Daylight is the safe plan.

faqs.q: Why does Lorenzi Park's page not mention pickleball?
faqs.a: The City does not say. Its post of 11 March 2026 counts "Four at Lorenzi Park"; the park's own page lists tennis courts, basketball courts, a band shell and a fishing pond, without pickleball. The record that states a number publishes, and the venue page says it rests on one record.

sources.evidence: The City's blog post "Play Pickleball in Las Vegas", dated March 11, 2026. "All ages can find their game by joining a league, dropping in or take skills classes at city courts this spring." "The city of Las Vegas has multiple courts to play on, and the spring season is here and ready for you." "Drop in for a pop-up game or sign up to be a part of a league and play in matches." Youth sports "offered in spring and fall" and adult sports leagues. Under "Where you can play": "The city's current pickleball court locations include: Two at Centennial Hills Park, Seven at Durango Hills Park, Eight at Police Memorial Park, Four at Bill Briare Park, Four at Lorenzi Park, Two at Patriot Park, Four at Justice Myron Leavitt & Jaycee Community Park, Four at Aloha Shores Park." Snapshot: data/sources/las-vegas/play-pickleball-in-las-vegas.html

History: "Lorenzi Park was the vision of David G. Lorenzi, a French immigrant who purchased 80 acres of property about two miles west of the original townsite in 1912. "Lorenzi Park is listed on the city's Historic Property Register as an historic district and on the Nevada State Register of Historic places."
